articles.title: Michigan Republican Tom Barrett Is Now Sour On Trump’s War in Iran—But Still Took Plenty of Defense Cash
articles.author: Julian Andreone
articles.summary: Rep. Tom Barrett (R-MI) departs the office of Speaker of the House Mike Johnson (R-LA) on August 31, 2026 in Washington, DC. Photo by Finn Gomez/Getty Images. While Republican Rep. Tom Barrett has been actively working to distance himself from President Donald Trump and the administration’s unpopular war in Iran, defense industry PACs and executives have poured more than $58,000 into Republican Rep. Tom Barrett’s bid for reelection in Michigan’s 7th district. He has also been on the happy end of at least a million dollars in super PAC support from Trump. Barrett broke with Trump over the Iran war in May after he repeatedly voted to support the war. In April, he cast a tie-breaking vote to defeat a war powers resolution aimed at ending it. The measure failed 214-213. Of the nearly $60,000 Barrett has received directly from the defense industry, $38,000 has come from defense contractors like Oracle, Lockheed Martin, Booz Allen Hamilton and General Dynamics.
